items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30-60 Day Post-Install Cohort)
items.preview:
**Why this first:** These 30 clients are in the satisfaction sweet spot (recently installed, system fresh, no service friction yet). Referral pushes are safe: no Concierge floor risk, no legacy-name landmines if I use the tenure line, and referrals are the sanctioned growth lever (Rule #3).
**1. Campaign name + audience:** "Know Anyone With Bad Water?". Referral Push · **30 recipients**
**2. Subject lines (all under 60 char):**
- Primary (specific): `$500 for a name. Here's how it works.`
- Curiosity: `The favor we only ask happy clients`
- Pain: `Your neighbor's water is probably worse than yours was`
- Authority: `Most of our best installs came from one thing`
- Specific: `Refer someone, get $500 (up to $1,000)`
**3. Preview text (under 90 char):** `No pressure. Just the simplest way we grow, and it pays you back.`
**4. Email body:**
> Hi [First Name],
>
> Quick one.
>
> It's been about a month since we installed your ClearWave system, and things should be running quietly in the background exactly the way they're supposed to.
>
> Here's the only favor we ever ask good clients: if you know someone fighting hard water, staining, or that funky taste, send them our way for a free water assessment.
>
> How it pays you:
>
> - If they become a client: **$500 cash** (goes up to $750 after your fifth referral, and $1,000 once you hit ten in a year).
> - If they just book the assessment and don't move forward: **$50 gift card**, no strings.
>
> Reply with a name and the best way to reach them, or forward this email to them directly. That's it.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
**5. Send timing:** **Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET.** Mid-morning Tuesday is the standard high-engagement window; avoids Monday inbox clearing.
**6. Expected performance:**
- Open: **40-45%** (in line with your 42.3% baseline; small, warm, recently-served list should hold near average).
- Click/reply: **3-6%.** Your click history is near zero, but those were promo blasts to the full 3,439. A targeted ask to a 30-person warm cohort with a clear single action ("reply with a name") reliably outperforms.
- Conversion: **1-2 booked consults** realistically from 30 recipients. Even one closed referral = $500 payout justifies the send.
**7. Source justification:** Draws from the **Referral push candidates (30-60 days post-install, satisfied)** Jobber trigger and the **Referral Bonus Structure** block. Uses the exact "free water assessment" phrase (Rule 3a) and the tenure line instead of any legacy name (Rule 2). Note: several systems in this cohort are legacy (Ironmax, H20 Protector), so I deliberately used the blanket "your ClearWave system" tenure framing.
---

items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge Upsell (13-24 Month Cohort)
items.preview:
**Why this second:** Largest qualified list (100), fully pre-filtered past the 12-month floor, and these clients have already experienced year-1 service so trust is established. Framed as a math question, not a pitch, per the Concierge voice guidance.
**1. Campaign name + audience:** "Is Concierge Worth It For Me?". Year 1.5 Upsell · **100 recipients** (dedupe note below)
> ⚠️ **Data flag:** Albert Romano appears twice (2/21 and 2/25/2025). Suppress duplicates before send or he gets two emails.
**2. Subject lines (all under 60 char):**
- Primary (specific): `The year-1.5 question: is Concierge worth it?`
- Curiosity: `Here's the math we run for clients like you`
- Pain: `Who's swapping your filters right now?`
- Authority: `What most clients ask us around 18 months`
- Specific: `$99/mo, and exactly what it covers`
**3. Preview text (under 90 char):** `Not a pitch. Just the honest math on whether Concierge pencils out for your home.`
**4. Email body:**
> Hi [First Name],
>
> It's been a little over a year since we installed your ClearWave system, so you've been through your first annual service and know how we work.
>
> Around this point, clients ask us the same thing: "Is this Concierge plan actually worth it for me?"
>
> Fair question. Here's the straight math.
>
> Concierge is $99/mo and covers:
>
> - Your annual service (already worth a chunk of that on its own)
> - Filter swaps handled for you, on schedule
> - Priority phone support (you skip the queue)
> - Parts coverage on your standard install components
>
> If you're the type who'd rather not track filter dates or price out parts one at a time, it usually pencils out. If you like handling it yourself, no problem, keep doing what works.
>
> Want me to run the numbers against your specific setup? Reply "math" and I'll send your breakdown.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
**5. Send timing:** **Thursday, 11:00 AM ET.** Spaced two days after Proposal 1 so no client on both lists gets hit back-to-back; late-morning midweek is strong for considered B2C reads.
**6. Expected performance:**
- Open: **38-43%.** Curiosity/math framing plus warm year-1.5 relationship should track baseline.
- Click/reply: **2-4%.** "Reply 'math'" is a low-friction micro-commitment that beats a link click.
- Conversion: **2-5 Concierge signups** at $99/mo = **$2,376-$5,940 annual recurring** from one send. Highest revenue potential of the two.
**7. Source justification:** Draws from **Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months post-install, NOT on Concierge)** trigger and the **Concierge Upsell Context** block (exact $99/mo terms, "is this worth it for me / here's the math" framing, non-pushy voice). Respects Rule #1: list is pre-filtered past 12 months, and copy uses the tenure line rather than naming legacy systems.
---
### Not proposed this week (and why)
- **Cold lead re-engagement (1,000):** High potential but needs a fresh water-news angle I don't have a verified source for right now. Rushing a stale hook to 1,000 cold contacts risks spam signals given your recent 0.2-0.4% open collapse. Worth a dedicated build next week.
- **1-year annual service (23):** Operational/service touch, lower revenue lift than referral + Concierge, and several are low-ticket ($349) accounts. Runs fine as an automated trigger rather than a featured campaign.
Want me to build out the cold-lead re-engagement for next week once we lock a news angle?

---
